question: Per-target-evaluation cost and end-to-end min-bulk-ESS per second of every Python call path of the owalnuts 0.2.0 wheel, and the ratio to nutpie 0.16.8 on the same PyMC models; then fix the worst actionable problem.

arm_definitions.py-numpy: plain Python callable written in idiomatic numpy (callpath_targets.numpy_target)
arm_definitions.py-njit: plain Python callable that calls the numba njit kernel shared with the cfunc arm (transport control)
arm_definitions.cfunc: owalnuts.from_cfunc of a numba cfunc calling the same njit kernel
arm_definitions.torch: owalnuts.from_torch(logp), CPU, default torch thread count
arm_definitions.pymc: owalnuts.from_pymc(model) (default PyTensor C backend; thread_safe=True when threads > 1, the documented rule)
arm_definitions.pymc-numba: owalnuts.from_pymc(model, mode='NUMBA') (same numba-compiled function as gil_free; thread_safe=True when threads > 1)
arm_definitions.nutpie: nutpie.compile_pymc_model(model) (numba backend), nutpie.sample(draws, tune, chains, cores=threads, seed)
arm_definitions.cfunc-guarded: amendment A2: the cfunc arm's njit kernel with the callable path's default nonfinite policy (zero gradient, return -inf)
arm_definitions.cfunc-safe: amendment A5: cfunc-guarded with the kernel and cfunc compiled with numba error_model='numpy'

sampler.settings: owalnuts.sample defaults (DEFAULTS); init=None (numpy uniform(-2,2) starts from seed); nutpie defaults

pytensor_compiledir_note: private compile cache: the shared per-user PyTensor compiledir lock is contended by sibling agents (a setup check blocked ~50 min on it)

baseline.source: wheel built by `maturin build --release` (GNU 1.88 toolchain) from 3583d130, installed non-editable

fix.source: wheel built by `maturin build --release` (GNU 1.88 toolchain) from commit 06a551a7 on wt/python-callpath, installed non-editable with numpy 2.4.6 (as in the baseline venv)

phase2.fix: F6 (pin one Python thread state per Rayon worker thread for a callable run; integrations/python/src/lib.rs ThreadStatePins) + F3 (from_jax passes the numpy position straight to the jitted function)
phase2.attribution: F6 acts only at threads=4 (threads=1 runs on the calling thread, which already has a Python thread state); F3 acts only on the jax arm. Judged: F3 on jax threads=1; F6 on py-numpy, py-njit, torch, pymc, pymc-numba at threads=4; jax threads=4 reported as the joint effect; every threads=1 cell is a no-regression check.

phase1c.note: amendment A5 supplementary phase, run after phase 2

order: strictly sequential child processes; micro cells first (targets outer, paths rotated per target); then seeds outer, targets, (arm x threads) list rotated by (3*seed_index + target_index); in phase 2 builds alternate inside each arm/threads pair

metrics.functionals: every unconstrained coordinate (rank-based bulk/tail ESS are invariant to the monotone constraining transforms, so nutpie's constrained draws give the same values) plus theta_1..theta_8 for eight
metrics.ess: owalnuts.summary (Rust diagnostics, matches ArviZ): minimum bulk ESS, minimum tail ESS, maximum rank R-hat
metrics.ess_per_second: min bulk ESS / wall of the owalnuts.sample or nutpie.sample call (construction and compilation excluded and reported separately); CONTENDED wall
metrics.ess_per_call: min bulk ESS / total target calls (owalnuts exact; nutpie warmup+draw n_steps)
metrics.per_call: micro: median of 10^4 individually timed calls through the Python surface (cfunc arms via ctypes, labelled) plus a decomposition into the raw compiled function; in-sampler: Rust wall / total target calls at threads=1
metrics.bit_identity: sha256 of the (chains, draws, dim) retained float64 draws

health: reported per cell: divergences, max-depth stops, R-hat <= 1.01, min bulk/tail ESS >= 400; failures reported not dropped

amendment_A1.frozen: 2026-10-24, after the harness smoke test and before the first phase-1 cell
amendment_A1.finding: from_pymc(thread_safe=True) at threads=4 recompiles the PyTensor function on (nearly) every callback: 349 compilations on 4 OS threads in ~8 min of a 4 x 30/30 probe

short_cells.other_seeds: recorded as status not_run_amendment_A1 (not run: a full cell would take days)

amendment_A1.new_candidate: F6: pin one Python thread state per Rayon worker thread for the duration of a callable run

decision_rule: A fix is worth merging iff (i) its retained draws are bit-identical (sha256) to the baseline build for every cell of every arm it touches, (ii) on at least one target the geometric mean over the three seeds of the paired fix/baseline ESS/s ratio (same arm, threads, seed, interleaved) is >= 1.3 for at least one touched arm/threads, and (iii) no touched arm/threads/target has that geometric mean below 0.9.

amendment_A3.frozen: 2026-10-24, after phase 1 and before phase 1b / phase 2
amendment_A3.change: phases phase1b and phase2 prime every oWALNUTS target with one evaluation at the zero vector before the timed sample call (lazy JIT compilation counted as construction)
amendment_A3.reason: phase-1 sampling walls of py-njit, jax, torch and pymc-numba include first-call JIT/lazy initialisation inside owalnuts.sample (the harness did not prime), contrary to the protocol's stated metric; phase-1 walls are reported as measured, labelled 'includes first-call compilation'
